item.title: Introducing This Master’s Thesis Blog
item.dc:creator: Johan
item.description:
This blog will work as a diary and progress report for my Master’s thesis. It is a place to show what I have done, keep track of how the work develops, and give myself something to look back on later. The first few posts will focus on stochastic filtering, with Fundamentals of Stochastic Filtering (Bain and Crisan 2009) as the main theoretical starting point and An Introduction to Sequential Monte Carlo (Chopin and Papaspiliopoulos 2020) as a complement for the computational methods that will be explored alongside the theory.

The early stage of the thesis is about building the right foundation: reviewing key ideas, connecting them to computational practice, and gradually moving toward more concrete questions related to the thesis itself. Later posts will therefore become more specific, following both my understanding of the subject and the actual development of the MSc thesis.

This blog is part my Master’s thesis for my Master of Science in Engineering degree in Risk, Safety and Crisis Management at Lund University. During my studies, I chose to take extra courses mainly in mathematical statistics, both at the engineering faculty and the faculty of science. These courses shape the way I approach the thesis, especially through probability theory, stochastic processes, mathematical modelling, and computational methods.

I also spent a year at UCSD, where I completed the course sequence for graduate students pursuing probability theory, an independent study course on stochastic differential equations, and a graduate course in computational stochastics, MATH 214, with a focus on applied aspects of SDEs.

The first posts may assume some familiarity with measure-theoretic probability theory, stochastic processes, and the basics of Monte Carlo simulations. At the same time, part of the purpose of this blog is to make the preparation visible. When I need to refresh or rebuild a theoretical idea, I will go back and work through the necessary parts carefully. Alongside the theoretical posts, I also expect to write about implementations, experiments, and computational examples, so much of the blog should still be approachable for readers with a basic background in probability.

Readers who want a sense of how I usually approach computational and mathematical problems can also look through some of my previous work on GitHub:

My GitHub repositories

A particularly relevant example is my exploration of computational methods for simulating SDEs in the MATH 214 course:

Project MATH 214

I look forward to using this blog to explore new areas of probability theory and its applications as the thesis develops!

References

Bain, Alan, and Dan Crisan. 2009. Fundamentals of Stochastic Filtering. Vol. 60. Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability. Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-76896-0.
Chopin, Nicolas, and Omiros Papaspiliopoulos. 2020. An Introduction to Sequential Monte Carlo. Springer Series in Statistics. Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-47845-2.
